Case report. Three years ago, we reported a 53-year old woman
with atypical SPS who presented with stiffness predominantly of
her right upper limb and trunk.
6 This case was unusual for MRI
findings of an intramedullary hyperintense lesion corresponding
to the site of the clinical symptoms. The neurologic symptoms of
the patient improved strikingly after initial treatment with IV
methylprednisolone and cyclophosphamide. After 3 years of im-
munosuppressive treatment, she showed no clinical signs of SPS
while taking methylprednisolone 6 mg/day by mouth.
Despite the initial presence of amphiphysin-autoantibodies in

the serum and CSF of the patient, we failed to detect a malig-
nancy. We therefore concluded that the patient’s SPS was not
paraneoplastic, particularly because amphiphysin-autoantibodies
were negative after immunosuppressive treatment. However,
more than 5 years after SPS onset, clinical and radiologic (mam-
mography, ultrasound, MRI) observation of a nonpalpable, small
nodule (1.5 /H110031.5 cm) in the right breast has led us to reconsider
this conclusion.
MRI-guided biopsy of the nodule revealed no malignancy at 3.5
years after onset of SPS. Yet, 1.5 years after that, the patient first
reported discomfort in her right breast, although no changes in
size or morphology suggesting malignancy could be detected by
imaging. Open surgery, however, unveiled an infiltrating ductal
carcinoma of the breast (size: 1.7 /H110031.2 /H110031 cm), which was
classified as moderately differentiated (G2; pT1c according to
UICC TNM classification). The tissue showed a strong expression
of amphiphysin at a molecular weight of 108 kD, as detected by
Western blot.
5 All of the 18 resected axillary lymph nodes were
tumor free and there was no evidence of metastatic spread. The
patient was therefore treated with tamoxifen and focal
radiotherapy.
